description:
Red Hills by Enza Developments is an exclusive resort-style real estate project located in the heart of Sahl Hasheesh on Egypt’s Red Sea coast. Designed with a modern architectural vision and a focus on luxury living, the development offers a harmonious blend of contemporary design and natural coastal beauty.

The project features a variety of unit types, including studios, apartments, penthouses, and chalets, all delivered with high-quality finishing and thoughtful layouts that maximize space, light, and comfort. Each residence is crafted to provide an elevated lifestyle experience, appealing to both end-users and investors.

Residents and visitors enjoy a comprehensive range of resort-level amenities, including multiple swimming pools, landscaped gardens, sports facilities, and dedicated leisure spaces. With 24/7 security, maintenance services, and smart living systems, Red Hills ensures convenience and peace of mind for all occupants.

Strategically positioned within minutes of pristine sandy beaches and just a short drive from Hurghada International Airport, Red Hills combines accessibility with the serenity of seaside living. This prime location enhances its appeal for vacation homes as well as long-term residential and rental investments.

With flexible payment plans and strong potential for capital appreciation, Red Hills by Enza Developments represents a compelling opportunity for those seeking a premium lifestyle destination or a strategic investment on the Red Sea.

description:
A project that drifts down from the serenity of the sky, forming like a cloud that hovers softly above

title: JuSuR, Competition, OMAN | MUSCAT
description:
In the heart of North Al-Seeb, along the rhythm of the Omani Sea waves, this project emerges as a contemporary urban vision that redefines the relationship between people and place. Here, buildings are not merely constructed—they are shaped as bridges: bridges between visitors and the land, between Oman’s maritime heritage and its touristic future, between the soul of the city and the modernity of the experience.

The project stretches as a continuous fabric connecting life and travel, stay and discovery, commerce and contemplation. In every path and every reflection in the water lies an invitation—to gather, to engage, to belong—whether for a fleeting visit or a lasting stay. It is not just a real estate development, but a sensory journey through light, water, and breathing spaces. And because it is envisioned for the Ministry of Tourism, its essence lies in crafting a civic platform where tourism is not a passing visit, but an immersive, holistic experience.

This project draws inspiration from Omani bridges — not merely as structural elements, but as profound symbols of connection, transition, and transformation. Just as bridges in Oman link the edges of valleys, just as the aflaj channels carry water across the terrain, and just as maritime piers stretch toward the horizon, the architectural masses of this project emerge as new urban bridges — connecting people to place, tourism to living, and the sea to the city. These are not merely architectural forms, but a spatial narrative that invites the visitor on a journey — from observation to belonging.

title: Osuol Towers, Competition, KSA
description:
In a land such as Al-Madinah Al-Munawwarah, architecture is not something imposed upon the soil; it is drawn forth from it, as meanings are drawn from the layers of ancient texts. The land itself becomes the source and the guide. When shafts of light pierce the depths of the earth, they awaken hidden forms within it, shaping stone masses that echo the very terrain from which they arise—raw, living presences that embody the continuity of time rather than imitate its traces. Each surface bears the memory of the ground, preserving its textures and colors, as if the buildings were an extension of the earth’s own history.

From within the rock, majestic trunks and columns emerge, as if grown from the heart of the land itself. These vertical forms rise not merely to support the weight of stone but to uphold a deeper concept and meaning. They stand like ancient trees that have broken through the crust of the earth, rooted firmly in the ground yet aspiring upward, bridging what lies below with what lies above. Their presence transforms the built environment into something at once organic and timeless, blurring the boundary between the natural and the man-made.

Each structure thus ascends in the spirit of the palm tree—anchored in the soil that nourishes it, yet reaching confidently toward the sky. The architecture becomes a living dialogue between earth and light, permanence and transcendence. It does not merely occupy the land but reveals it, shaping a place that honors both the physical ground and the cultural memory it holds. In this way, the built form becomes not a foreign object placed on the earth, but a natural outgrowth of the land itself, carrying forward its essence while opening new paths toward the horizon.

The project adopts a Tree-Column structural system as a transitional framework, carrying the loads from the upper floors down to the base of the building. Inspired by the trunks of trees, this approach reflects the project’s profound connection to the land from which it rises. Here, the columns are not conceived as mere structural elements; they transform into living trunks, emerging from the depths of the rock and rising quietly to support the mass above, just as a tree carries the gentle weight of its own shade.

This structural concept enables the organic distribution of loads, echoing the way roots spread naturally through the soil to anchor and nourish the tree. By transferring forces efficiently, it allows for open, unobstructed interior spaces, enhancing the sense of lightness and continuity within the building. The absence of heavy internal barriers invites movement, visual connection, and spatial freedom—qualities that reinforce the building’s dialogue with its natural setting.

The branching form of the Tree-Columns also creates natural pathways for light and air to permeate the interior, reducing reliance on mechanical systems for ventilation and illumination. In doing so, the architecture affirms itself as a living entity, one that breathes with and responds to its environment rather than imposing itself as a static, inert mass. The result is a structure that feels both grounded and alive—rooted in the earth, yet open to the rhythms of light, air, and the passage of time.
